A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from StreamOcc to DuOcc. All 14 pages of v1.pdf and 16 pages of v2.pdf, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original occupancy and detection results, component ablations, qualitative predictions and appendix RayIoU evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds SurroundOcc evaluation, supervision ablations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: v2 adds training-only forecasting and occupied-mask supervision heads to the existing RefineNet, with corresponding losses absent from v1's four-term objective (Section 3.1; Appendix A.4). This is a targeted training modification; the recurrent voxel aggregation, QueryAgg and inference pipeline remain essentially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds SurroundOcc evaluation alongside Occ3D-nuScenes. Its wider LiDAR-coordinate volume and 0.5 m voxels extend spatial and annotation coverage beyond the retained ego-coordinate, 0.4 m benchmark, within the same autonomous-driving occupancy task. The appendix's urban, rainy and occluded scenarios were already present in v1.

E2.justification: The comparison set expands substantially: v2 Table 1 adds two separately cited entries labeled ProtoOcc, and the matched RayIoU comparison adds ODG. The new SurroundOcc comparison includes previously unevaluated TPVFormer, GaussianFormer, GaussianFormer-2 and GaussianWorld, broadening the competing representation families.

E3.justification: The added SurroundOcc experiment uses 20 training epochs, class-agnostic IoU and RTX 4090 timing; existing Occ3D training remains at 24 epochs. v2 also reports FLOPs and parameter counts. Table 1 changes its strict 100 ms real-time grouping to approximately 100 ms, including a 105 ms comparator.

E4.justification: v1 Table 3 isolates bottleneck convolution and 3D-CBAM; v2 Table 5 replaces that breakdown with RefineNet and successive forecasting/occupied-mask supervision ablations. Appendix B.1 adds computational-cost analysis. The detector/QueryAgg ablations and qualitative case studies are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. Results remain point estimates without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds SurroundOcc results of 33.4 IoU and 23.0 mIoU, new comparator scores, and profiling results of 418 GFLOPs and 49M parameters. Reported full-model memory changes from 2,011 to 2,788 MB, and StreamAgg-only memory from 1,829 to 2,437 MB; FastOcc latency changes from 93.4 to 90.3 ms. Ablation entries are replaced under revised supervision configurations, and the per-class 'others' column disappears. Headline Occ3D mIoU of 41.9 and RayIoU of 41.1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 11 substantively expands the defined training objective with forecasting and binary-occupancy losses. The additional CBAM equations explain an already described component, while the warping and query-attention mathematics remain equivalent. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The headline memory-saving claim is narrowed from over 50% to over 40%, and the stated benchmark scope extends from Occ3D-nuScenes to include SurroundOcc. The central claims of efficient dense streaming, query-guided dynamic-object refinement and joint detection remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes temporal consistency and occupied/free-space discrimination specifically to the new forecasting and occupied-mask supervision. Appendix B.1 adds explanations connecting competitors' architectures to FLOPs and parameter costs. Existing interpretations concerning motion misalignment, occlusion and complementary voxel/query features are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies auxiliary-head targets, loss types and weights of 10.0, and clarifies the mask decoder's group-wise assignment and training-only use. However, it omits v1's explicit 700/150 scene counts, 256-channel downsampled feature width and attention kernel size of 7. These omissions do not establish changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially expanded around Gaussian representations and stream-based 3D perception, positioning DuOcc as an adaptation of dense recurrent perception to occupancy prediction. New references include RecurrentBEV, OnlineBEV, Sparse4D v2 and GaussianWorld. One added citation, reference 47, concerns ECG-based QT prolongation despite being cited as stream-based 3D perception.

P1.justification: The title and model name change, and existing abstract, introduction, method and experimental prose are extensively rewritten. Related work gains a dedicated streaming subsection, experiments are reorganized into seven subsections, and implementation details receive numbered appendix subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the accuracy/memory plot with a conceptual comparison of dense, sparse and streaming approaches. Module diagrams are consolidated into Figure 2, and Figure 3 now details RefineNet supervision. Tables are substantially reformatted, RayIoU moves into the main text, new benchmark/profiling tables appear, and qualitative panels are reordered.

improvement.justification: The SurroundOcc evaluation, targeted supervision ablations and computational profiling strengthen validation, while the revised method explanation clarifies training. These provide a modest net improvement despite lost implementation details and reporting errors. For example, v2 claims more than fourfold lower memory than COTR, but Table 1 gives 10,453 versus 2,788 MB, approximately 3.75-fold; the substantial memory revisions are also unexplained.
